bullets.title: META down ~6% as CDS hits record; capex language spooks markets despite Muse beat
bullets.body: META's 5-year CDS spread hit an all-time high of 114.5bps as tech credit spreads widened broadly on AI debt concerns. Despite a strong Q3 ($64.6B revenue, +26.1% YoY, beating consensus) and Muse reaching 10M+ users with 25% DAU, investor focus shifted to 'hundreds of billions' capex language and a Class C equity raise signaled for January 2027. Full-year 2026 capex narrowed to $135-145B (87-101% YoY growth); 2027 capex guidance deferred to Q4 call.

bullets.title: Broad tape: S&P +1.3%, VIX +15.4% to 19.25; 10yr at 5.03%, crude +2.5% to $99.61
bullets.body: Pre-market showed S&P 500 futures up ~75pts (+0.95%) to 7,726 while the 10-year Treasury yield rose 9bps to 5.03% and WTI crude jumped $2.46 (+2.53%) to $99.61. By mid-morning, StreetAccount reported S&P 500 cash up 1.3% to 7,653.99 with VIX surging 15.4% to 19.25, reflecting simultaneous risk-on equity tape and vol/rates stress — a cross-asset tension consistent with AI capex uncertainty.

bullets.title: Fed reaction function: slow to respond to AI capex fears; yield curve to flatten
bullets.body: Multiple strategists (22V, Hedgeye) argue the Fed will not cut on AI capex concerns in 2028+ as long as inflation stays above 2%, growth exceeds the ~2% speed limit, and 2027 capex plans are met — all three conditions currently hold. Consensus expects no Fed change at October meeting (94% probability) with December pricing 74% for a 25bp hike. 10yr yields are seen as driven by downside risk to $7 trillion cumulative AI capex consensus; yield curve flattening is the base case, favoring risk-averse factors and long PFIX positioning.

bullets.title: AI capex debate: 2027 plans intact, 2028+ uncertainty is the real risk
bullets.body: Strategists at Citi and 22V note that AI capex concerns are about 2028 and beyond, not 2027 — hyperscaler 2027 capex is expected to deliver a ~70-80bp GDP impulse with high conviction. Citi separately argues AI's capital demand is large enough to move r-star higher globally, prompting central banks to rethink neutral-rate assumptions. The risk scenario is an AI equity decline cutting off infrastructure funding, not a near-term capex pullback.

bullets.title: Semis broadly selling off: LRCX -10%, iShares Semi ETF -4.3%; AMAT/KLAC -6% in sympathy
bullets.body: Lam Research fell 10.1% post-earnings with an inline guide attributed to supply chain constraints rather than demand weakness; analysts at Klein note 2027 WFE growing >29% YoY with DRAM/logic/NAND tailwinds and view the selloff as sentiment overshooting. AMAT and KLAC fell ~6.2% in sympathy, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF dropped 4.27%. Electronic Technology sector logged 0 new 52-week highs vs. 12 lows.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler margin divergence: non-hyperscaler AI beneficiaries still upgrading estimates
bullets.body: Quant analysis shows hyperscaler NTM earnings estimates have plateaued since late August and declined 0.6% in September (first drop since Feb 2023), driven by rising depreciation as AI infrastructure enters service. Meanwhile, non-hyperscaler AI beneficiaries continue to see EPS estimate upgrades and the broadest guidance raises in the Technology sector. Excluding GOOGL and META from Communications cuts estimated sector margins by more than half.

bullets.title: Hedgeye AI framework: more shorts than 2 weeks ago; memory stocks 'second layer to break'
bullets.body: Keith McCullough exited QQQ, rotated into MSFT-linked income ETF (MSFY), added to Russell 2000 short, shorted South Korea (EWY), and maintained DRAM and India shorts. He characterizes the S&P 500 downside/upside at ~2:1 and identifies memory stocks as the second layer to break in the AI framework after neoclouds. Amazon moved to the buy column while Blackstone and Carlyle were shorted.

bullets.title: Initial claims fell to 194k, 4-week avg at 198k (4-year low); labor market stays resilient
bullets.body: Weekly initial jobless claims fell 6k to 194k, with the 4-week moving average declining 1k to 198k — a four-year low. Continuing claims rose 25k to 1,728k. UBS favors PAYC over temp staffing plays (EFOR, RHI) heading into earnings on this data, and strategists cite strong consumer spending in October as reinforcing the slow-Fed-reaction thesis.

bullets.title: Euro area consumer confidence slips to -17.9; JPMorgan cuts H2 consumption forecast
bullets.body: Euro area household confidence fell 1.4pts to -17.9 in October after a 1.0pt decline in September, with record fuel prices cited as the key drag. JPMorgan lowered H2 2026 household consumption growth to 0.75% annualized from 0.9%, flagging that the confidence-spending relationship has recently weakened vs. historical patterns.

bullets.title: GS Prime: short leverage near 5-year highs; short-interest basket at lows creates asymmetric upside
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs Prime Brokerage reports short sales outpaced long buys 5:1 month-to-date, with short leverage near five-year highs. The high short-interest basket (GSCBMSAL) is materially below 2026 highs with a 14-day RSI that briefly dipped below 30. GS recommends a call strategy on the basket for asymmetric upside participation.

bullets.title: Credit card quality improving Y/Y: avg delinquencies -31bps, NCOs -42bps in September
bullets.body: September 2026 credit card data showed average delinquency rates improved 31bps Y/Y (median -10bps) and average NCO rates fell 42bps Y/Y (median -37bps). Delinquencies reflect conditions ~60 days prior and losses lag by ~6 months, meaning improvement trends still have runway into 2027.

bullets.title: Mortgage rates at 7.40% (highest since Nov 2023); LIRA forecasts remodeling to nearly stall in 1Q27
bullets.body: The Leading Indicator of Remodeling Activity projects homeowner improvement spending growth slowing sharply to +0.5% in Q1 2027 and +0.6% in Q2 2027, down from +2.4% for full-year 2026. With mortgage rates at 7.40% (highest since November 2023), housing starts declining, and remodeling permits stagnant, housing has effectively exited as an active business cycle participant.

bullets.title: AI reclassifying the enterprise software landscape: open-weight models threatening SaaS incumbents
bullets.body: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna and Palo Alto's Nikesh Arora warned that open-weight AI models could capture 75-90% of enterprise AI token consumption at 10-40x lower costs, substantially disrupting traditional SaaS businesses. AI platforms combining reasoning, memory, and applications could increase switching costs for hyperscaler-adjacent tools while pressuring independent software vendors. Quantum computers are expected to threaten current encryption around 2030.

bullets.title: Prediction markets: no Oct Fed change (94%), Dec hike 74%; Democrat sweep 68%
bullets.body: Prediction market consensus shows 94% probability of no Fed change at the October meeting and 74% probability of a 25bp hike in December. On policy, a Democrat sweep in the 2026 midterms is priced at 68%, with Democrats at 92% to win the House and 68% for the Senate. WTI oil has a 79% probability of finishing the year at $80+ and 42% at $100+.

bullets.title: TXN Q3 strong beat; GM of 64.2% vs 61.2% est; Dec guide EPS $2.62 vs $2.30 cons
bullets.body: Texas Instruments reported Q3 revenue of $6.06B vs. consensus $5.92B with gross margin of 64.2% vs. the 61.2% estimate. December quarter EPS guidance of $2.62 was well above the $2.30 consensus. Analysts note 2027-28 consensus GMs of ~64% assume flat expansion from Q3 despite 15% higher quarterly revenue — likely conservative — with AI data center growing ~100% YoY being GM-accretive.

bullets.title: SPOT +7-8% on Q3 premium sub beat; Q4 GM guide 33.8% above Street; AI costs moderating
bullets.body: Spotify Q3 showed premium subscriber additions exceeding expectations with Q3 revenue €4.97B (+14% YoY) and free cash flow €735M. Q4 guidance of €5.2B revenue and €820M operating income surprised to the upside, with gross margin guide of 33.8% beating Morgan Stanley's 33.5%. AI investment costs are expected to moderate into Q4 2026 and 2027, with token cost cuts and model routing driving productivity gains.

bullets.title: TSLA North American FSD attach >75% (+20ppt q/q); Robotaxi autonomous miles +30% w/w
bullets.body: Tesla's North American FSD attach rates exceeded 75%, up 20 percentage points quarter-over-quarter, with paid FSD customers above 1.7M. Robotaxi autonomous miles reached ~558k per week with ~30% week-over-week growth since Q3 end. Morgan Stanley raised its Tesla price target to $410 from $400 citing Cybercab deployment scaling 10x and four new city launches.

bullets.title: NFLX Q4 guide misses on revenue and operating income; first FY below starting guidance in 3 years
bullets.body: Netflix Q3 beat on content timing, but Q4 guidance came in below the Street on both revenue and operating income. FY26 is expected to finish below starting guidance for the first time in three years. Ad revenue came in at ~$2.7B vs. ~$3B expected; management attributes the shortfall to slower rollout pacing, not demand. A leadership change at Chief Content Officer (Peter Rice replacing Bela Bajaria) was framed as an execution reset.

bullets.title: CMCSA Q3 beats on EBITDA/EPS/FCF but broadband deteriorates; Orlando parks drag into H1 2027
bullets.body: Comcast Q3 revenue of $29.3B and EBITDA of $9.1B beat expectations, with EPS of $1.07 vs. consensus $0.97. However, broadband net adds of -144k missed, ARPU declined 2.9%, and wireless adds of +368k were below the ~400k consensus. Theme park softness (especially Orlando) is expected to persist through H1 2027; a $1B+ transformation charge is coming in Q4. NBCUniversal/Sky separation is on track for mid-2027.

bullets.title: AI data center buildout faces rising headwinds: power mandates, local opposition, higher rates
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag structural cost pressures for AI infrastructure: Trump administration is demanding data centers generate their own power and pay local communities; UK local opposition threatens Microsoft's $30B AI infrastructure investment; UBS experts cite power delivery timeline constraints, regulatory pushback, and higher interest rates complicating project financing. States are expected to impose data-center moratoriums and slower permitting timelines.
